what_its_for: Megestrol is used to help improve appetite and cause weight gain in people with serious illnesses such as cancer or HIV/AIDS who have lost a lot of weight. It may also be used to treat certain types of breast or uterine (endometrial) cancer.
how_to_take: Take megestrol by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device that comes with your medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your dose will depend on why you are taking this medicine. For appetite and weight gain, the usual dose of the regular liquid (40 mg/mL) is 800 mg once a day, or it may be divided into smaller doses taken throughout the day. The concentrated liquid (Megace ES, 625 mg/5 mL) is usually taken as one 5 mL teaspoon (625 mg) once a day. For cancer treatment, doses and schedules vary. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store megestrol at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not freeze the liquid form. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking megestrol, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some can interact with megestrol. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and talk to your doctor about your options. Do not stop taking megestrol suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you have: sudden chest pain or shortness of breath (which could be a blood clot), severe pain, redness, or swelling in your leg, sudden severe headache or vision changes, signs of a blood sugar problem (increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision), signs of an adrenal problem such as unusual tiredness, dizziness, nausea, or weakness, vaginal bleeding that is unusual or unexpected, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing, or any new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: For appetite improvement and weight gain, you may begin to notice some changes within a few weeks, but it may take 4 to 8 weeks to see the full benefit. For cancer treatment, your doctor will monitor your response over time. Keep taking megestrol even if you do not feel different right away — do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially blood clots and adrenal problems. Your doctor will monitor you carefully. Pregnancy: Do NOT use megestrol if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm to the baby. Use effective contraception during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking megestrol. It may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose or monitoring may need to be adjusted. Diabetes: Megestrol may raise blood sugar levels. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar closely and report any changes to your doctor.
